record.original_question: For a holomorphic foliation on complex projective space, possibly with singularities, must every leaf accumulate at a singular point of the foliation?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation by curves on the complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ (in particular, one may take $n=2$). By definition, $\mathcal{F}$ is given by an open cover $\{U_i\}$ of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ together with holomorphic vector fields $X_i$ on $U_i$, with isolated zeros, such that on each overlap $U_i\cap U_j$ one has $X_i = g_{ij} X_j$ for some nowhere-vanishing holomorphic function $g_{ij}$. The singular set $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ is the (finite) set of zeros of these local vector fields. Off $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$, the integral curves of the $X_i$ glue into a holomorphic foliation whose maximal connected immersed holomorphic curves are called the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$.

Question: Must every leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$ have a singular point of $\mathcal{F}$ in its closure? Equivalently, does $\overline{L}\cap\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})\neq\varnothing$ hold for every leaf $L$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every leaf of a holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ (even on $\mathbb{CP}^2$) must accumulate at a singular point is widely cited as a basic open problem in the theory of holomorphic foliations. Recent surveys on global dynamics and singularities of holomorphic foliations continue to list this as an unresolved question, and no proof or counterexample appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Global dynamics and perspectives on singularities of holomorphic foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing open dynamical questions about singular holomorphic foliations on projective spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey treats accumulation/dynamics questions for foliations on projective spaces as ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on foliations on CP^n with a unique singular point
status_evidence.snippet: Studies leaves and singular points of foliations on projective spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on the relationship between leaves and singular points without resolving the general accumulation question.
